hero.title: The constitution release.
hero.lede: Three goals in priority order now decide what stays in the tree: credentials are unleakable, one trace is complete, and a capability arrives as a Wasm component. Everything that served none of them is gone, the audit file included.

summary: The rule is unchanged: the model proposes, the separate broker authorizes. What changed is where the record lives. Audit is a log record on the message’s W3C trace, and there is no metadata-only mode to hide the rest of it.

highlights.title: Secret bytes exist only inside the broker.
highlights.body: The native HTTP engine injects a credential after the component has built its request, and now refuses a response that echoes it on every credential kind, bearerToken included. A bearer secret under 16 printable bytes refuses startup, so the echo check can’t deny unrelated responses.
points: The echo check covers bearerToken and chatgptSubscription, not only DRN-bound secrets
Telegram errors render without the token-bearing URL
Chat transports and the OTLP exporter refuse an ambient proxy

highlights.title: Everything an agent did is on one W3C trace.
highlights.body: The trace opens at transport.receive, before the payload is parsed. Everything rides it as spans or log records: prompts, scripts, command words, broker decisions, HTTP egress. The audit record is one of those log records; there is no audit file.
points: telemetryPayloads and every metadata-only mode are gone
The separate Dekopon trace id is gone; traceParent is mandatory
The 256-span cap is gone; a span is never dropped

highlights.title: A command word can behave like a real CLI.
highlights.body: dekopon:provider@0.3.0 adds the provider-cli world. run-command receives argv plus the piped value and answers with one of three things: a capability proposal, text it rendered itself such as --help, or a decline. The broker host also links a grant-free wall clock, readable during invoke only.
points: An optional clap layer in the SDK, compiled without env or color
FakeBroker::run_command drives a word through the real broker host

path.title: From transport receipt to HTTP egress.
path.body: Every span and log record carries the same trace id. The broker parents its spans on the request’s traceParent, and a gateway that exports nothing still mints one so a decision record can be found.
path.ariaLabel: The spans and records one Dekopon message leaves on its trace

steps.name: broker.decision
steps.detail: Cedar’s answer and its policy ids

changes.title: Audit is one log record per broker decision, inside the trace.
changes.body: broker.decision and broker.execution go to stdout as JSON always, and to OTLP logs when telemetry names a receiver. auditPath, checkpointPath, and audit verify are gone; an existing audit.jsonl is inert. Losing the exporter loses the audit.

changes.title: There is no metadata-only mode.
changes.body: telemetryPayloads is refused by name. Always exported now: input on broker.authorize and provider.invoke, url.full on http.request, and the prompt, answer, script, and output records. Secret bytes, the gateway’s own credentials, and HTTP headers and bodies never were.

changes.title: Idempotency, the replay ledger, and the namespace key are deleted.
changes.body: idempotency: is an unknown field in constraintSets and manifests, and a resubmitted invocation runs again. Storage names are unkeyed SHA-256 now, so provider storage starts empty at upgrade: stop the broker and move the root aside.

changes.title: kind: Provider and kind: Capability are gone.
changes.body: Nothing read them at runtime. The surface a session reaches is the broker’s answer under the agent’s attestation, built from loaded manifests and the constraintSets policy allows. A catalog that still carries either kind refuses to load and names the upgrade.

changes.title: run-command replaces resolve-command.
changes.body: A word gets its argv and the piped value, and may render its own help page at exit 0 without charging a capability call. Components built against provider 0.1.0 or 0.2.0 keep loading; their legacy export never receives a piped value.

link.label: Expose a provider as a shell word

changes.title: An agent reads SKILL.md directories on demand.
changes.body: spec.skills lists Agent Skills directories. The model sees names and descriptions, reads a body or one resource with read_skill, and each read is one agent.skill.read record. Skill text is untrusted model text and grants nothing.

changes.title: chatgptSubscription is a broker credential kind.
changes.body: The broker refreshes it 60 seconds before expiry through the one implementation in dekopon-model, under an advisory lock, and never charges the renewal to the invocation. Give the broker its own auth file: sharing one with the gateway revokes the token family for both.

link.label: See how credentials reach the broker

changes.title: Two executables: dekopond and dekopon-brokerd.
changes.body: Retired: dekopon, dekopon-webui, dekopon-run, and dekopon-provider-host. dekopond auth chatgpt takes over the model-account login, and dekopon-brokerd probe is the readiness check. The console lives on in the dekopon-console repository.

changes.title: Rust 1.98.1, Wasmtime 48, wit-bindgen 0.62, wasm-tools 1.259.
changes.body: Each pin lives in one place and every repository-owned fixture is rebuilt on the stack. The WIT didn’t change, so components built on the older toolchain keep loading.

detailsIntro: A change is judged by which goal it serves. A subsystem that serves none is a deletion candidate, however well built.

telemetry.title: authority moved to the gateway, console, or model
telemetry.body: Cedar, the credentials, and the audit record all stay inside the separate broker. What moved is where the record lives: on the trace, not in a file.
telemetry.note: A compromised gateway can vouch for any subject in its attestor lane. Dekopon remains pre-production.

packages.name: Homebrew
packages.body: The generated formula installs both executables from the attested release archives.

packages.name: crates.io
packages.body: The release workflow publishes the provider SDK, its testkit, and every other public crate at the application version. Pin the exact version.

packages.name: Container
packages.body: The Debian 13 distroless multi-architecture image carries both executables and the pinned provider components.

installIntro: Current install paths: Homebrew, crates.io, the attested archives, and the multi-architecture image. The published Helm chart trails the application.

current: Credentials are unleakable: secret bytes exist only inside the broker
One trace, complete: audit is a log record on the message’s W3C trace
Extensible through Wasm providers: provider-cli command words, a wall clock, and skills
Two executables, the public crates, and a multi-architecture image

Argument values on shell.command spans, not only their count

scopeIntro: The whole local path works today, from transport receipt to an audited HTTP call. The chart with separate gateway and broker UIDs exists in source and is not yet published.
